ABSTRACT

The Ciliwung River Basin has a serious environmental problem of water quality deterioration due to growing urbanization, domestic wastewater and industrial activity. The current conventional monitoring methods still face the problems of limited real-time information, early warning capabilities and long-term sustainability, especially under the budgetary and technical limits of many developing countries. This paper provides a regionally customized design framework for an online water quality monitoring system considering technological feasibility and social, economic and environmental requirements. The novelty of this work is the design of a context-specific monitoring system that optimizes reliability, affordability and a high domestic component utilization (local content) simultaneously, which is rarely addressed in prior works that focus mainly on technical performance only. The study adopted a mixed methods approach that included community perception surveys, in-depth stakeholder interviews, descriptive analysis of existing technologies, cost-benefit analysis, and system development utilizing the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) methodology. The results indicate that the suggested system design may successfully suit the local operational requirements, enhance the continuity and accuracy of water quality monitoring, and provide a practical early warning mechanism for pollution events in the major river basins. This study offers a reproducible and scalable methodology for constructing online monitoring systems in resource-constrained contexts, providing a bridge between state-of-the-art sensor technology and local implementation capacity. The suggested approach is a feasible technology basis from a policy point of view for boosting national water pollution control programs, early warning systems and data-driven river basin management. The findings thus encourage the integration of locally tailored online monitoring tools into national water resource protection programs to promote sustainable water governance in Indonesia and other similar developing regions.
